## Purpose and Entry Points
LenovoLegionLinux provides Linux hardware support and controls for Lenovo Legion laptops: EC-backed fan curves and sensors, firmware settings, and platform power profiles. The primary runtime is an out-of-tree kernel module at `kernel_module/legion-laptop.c`, built/loaded via `kernel_module/Makefile`. User-facing entry points are the Python CLI and GUI at `python/legion_linux/legion_linux/legion_cli.py` and `python/legion_linux/legion_linux/legion_gui.py`.

## Kernel Hardware Driver
`kernel_module/legion-laptop.c` is the architectural core. It probes supported DMI/BIOS combinations, interfaces with laptop ACPI/embedded-controller mechanisms, and protects model-specific features through allowlists. `kernel_module/Makefile` supports build, install, reload, DKMS-related, and kernel-patch workflows; `kernel_module/dkms.conf` enables rebuilds against new kernels.

## Linux Interface Boundary
The driver translates proprietary firmware/EC operations into standard Linux kernel interfaces: hwmon sensor and PWM fan-curve attributes, debugfs fan-curve inspection, sysfs feature controls, and ACPI platform-profile integration. This is the central compatibility boundary: desktop tools and scripts consume kernel-standard files rather than hardware protocols. The driver also exposes controls such as fan lock/unlock, charge conservation, Fn lock, touchpad, and related model-dependent settings.

## Python Control Layer
`python/legion_linux/legion_linux/legion.py` centralizes discovery and reading/writing of the driver’s sysfs/hwmon/debugfs interfaces, plus applicable existing kernel interfaces. It is the shared domain/API layer for both front ends. `legion_cli.py` offers scriptable commands, while the PyQt GUI in `legion_gui.py` edits, applies, imports, and persists fan-curve presets. Both require appropriate privileges because their writes ultimately target kernel control files.

## Profile Automation Daemon
The C-based `legiond` service monitors power source and platform-profile state with inotify, selects a matching AC/battery fan preset, and applies it to hardware. Its composition is visible in `extra/service/legiond/legiond.c`, `extra/service/legiond/modules/setapply.c`, and `extra/service/legiond/modules/powerstate.c`. Service integration supports systemd/OpenRC through `extra/service/legiond.service` and companion files; example policy/profile data resides in `extra/service/profiles/`. Optional configured actions invoke external CPU/GPU tuning tools such as RyzenADJ, Intel undervolting utilities, `nvidia-smi`, or `rocm-smi`.

## Alternative SmartFan Path
For Legion 7 Gen 10+ systems, SmartFan is an independent shell-service path that uses `acpi_call` rather than the full kernel module. `extra/smartfan/smartfan.sh` implements control behavior, `extra/smartfan/smartfan.service` integrates it with systemd, and `extra/smartfan/workmode.sh` provides mode selection. It is a separate hardware-control boundary, not a frontend over the standard driver interfaces.

## Delivery and Runtime Infrastructure
Distribution packaging spans native package specs and Python packaging under `deploy/build_packages/`, while containerized build/test environments cover Arch, Fedora, SUSE, and Ubuntu in `deploy/`. GitHub Actions workflows in `.github/workflows/build.yml` and release automation validate and publish deliverables. Runtime dependencies materially include a compatible Linux kernel/headers, DKMS where used, PyQt and YAML for Python UI/configuration, systemd or OpenRC for automation, and optional `acpi_call` or GPU/CPU vendor tools.
